Model-first structure: the axis-locking heuristic is explained before the property (the reader must understand railing to understand the opt-out), including the PR's own 500px/3px worked example and the gesture-scoped persistence rule. Why-it-exists covers the JavaScript workaround costs (main-thread latency, scroll-feature interference) with explainer citations; the touch-action rejection rationale (semantic mismatch + input modality) is included because it is the question every reader asks.

Three semantic pre/code examples: the explainer's canonical 2D map viewport (verbatim pattern), a swipe-to-dismiss card, and an @supports progressive-enhancement guard. No live iframe: the showcase route HEAD-checks 404 (2026-07-29) and a meaningful demo needs real gesture input — the page states both facts honestly instead of embedding a broken frame. Examples are CSS-declarative and cannot be executed headlessly to confirm the unlocked behavior; runtime verification needs a touch/wheel-capable session.

No BCD entry and no web-features entry (both verified absent with linked queries, 2026-07-29) — the compat table is labelled interim and compiled from the milestone listing, the trunk flag record (experimental status disclosed against the EBD listing), the intent rollout plan, and the two standards-positions issues. Unsupported-browser fallback (declaration ignored → default behavior) and an @supports guard are documented in the errors section.

Every visible citation label is a direct link: PR files view, issue-comment anchors, explainer anchors, both Chromium source files, intent msgid, WPT blob + wpt.fyi results, both chromestatus endpoints, css-syntax-3 and css-overflow-3 anchors, TAG review, both positions issues, BCD tree, webstatus API, crbug, showcase route. Zero plain-text source labels. External links carry target=_blank rel=noopener.

The property's own accessibility dimension is a first-class page section (the heuristic exists to help users who cannot swipe straight; opt-in default + unidirectional-container safety + author guidance on when none is a deliberate UX trade-off) — drawn verbatim-in-substance from the explainer's accessibility section. Page itself: semantic h1>h2 hierarchy, th-scoped tables, banner role=note, code tokens wrap rather than clip.

All six tables inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; first column capped at 30%/7.5rem; long tokens (flag names, msgid URLs) covered by overflow-wrap:anywhere on code cells; pre blocks scroll internally; h1/lede wrap anywhere. Verified by headless-Chromium screenshots at 390px and 1280px, read after capture (see report).

Showcase feature route HEAD-checked: 404 (2026-07-29) — per the Case B rule the page uses a text link plus pre/code snippets and states the 404 explicitly, rather than embedding a broken iframe. The see-also entry points at the showcase feature URL for when a demo lands.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data tables reference documentation no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing and the browser layout engine; keep overflow contained (wrapping containers with overflow-x:auto for wide tables, overflow-wrap anywhere for unbreakable tokens, internal scrolling for code blocks) rather than fixed pixel widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} around all six tables; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1/lede/table code; pre{overflow-x:auto} so grammar/IDL scrolls internally; no hardcoded table widths beyond a 30% first-column cap with rem minimum. Screenshots at 390px/1280px read to confirm.
